title: serve-web: /web-extension-resource always returns 403, so no web extension can be installed from the Extensions panel
body:

<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->

- VS Code Version: 1.134.0-insider (`server-linux-x64-web`, commit `fc62850c022bbba2c93b0202dd24f42d1e0b3882`). Also reproduced on stable 1.133.0.
- OS Version: Linux x64 (server); browser-independent

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Download and unpack the current insider web server build:

   ```
   curl -sL "$(curl -s https://update.code.visualstudio.com/api/update/server-linux-x64-web/insider/latest | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["url"])')" | tar xz
   ```

2. Start it: `./bin/code-server-insiders serve-local --port 8080 --host 127.0.0.1 --without-connection-token --accept-server-license-terms`

3. Request any marketplace asset through the extension-resource proxy:

   ```
   curl -i 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/web-extension-resource/google.vscode-unpkg.net/google/reflowlist/0.8.1/extension/package.json'
   ```

Expected: `200`, with the asset proxied from `https://google.vscode-unpkg.net/...`.

Actual: `403 Request Forbidden`, returned in ~1.5ms with no outbound request made. Fetching the same
URL directly from the same host returns `200` (3576 bytes), so this is not network, egress or
marketplace availability.

In a browser this surfaces as every web extension (one declaring `browser` in its manifest) failing
to install from the Extensions panel with `403 Request Forbidden`.

### Cause

`WebClientServer.handle` in `src/vs/server/node/webClientServer.ts` matches the route prefix, checks
the next character is a slash, and then does not step over it. From the shipped bundle
(`out/server-main.js`, identifiers are minifier output, `uC` is `"/web-extension-resource"`):

```js
o.startsWith(uC) && o.charCodeAt(uC.length) === 47
  ? this._handleWebExtensionResource(t, e, o.substring(uC.length))
  : ...
```

So `_handleWebExtensionResource` receives
`/google.vscode-unpkg.net/google/reflowlist/0.8.1/extension/package.json`, with the leading slash
still attached. It then splits that into an authority and a path at the first slash:

```js
authority: i.substring(0, i.indexOf("/")),
path:      i.substring(i.indexOf("/") + 1)
```

Because the leading slash survived, `indexOf("/")` is 0, the authority is the empty string, and the
whole thing lands in the path. `_getResourceURLTemplateAuthority` returns `undefined` for that empty
authority while returning `vscode-unpkg.net` for the template, the two do not match, and the next
line returns 403 before fetching anything.

Instrumenting the bundle confirms it:

```
parsed={"scheme":"https","authority":"","path":"/google.vscode-unpkg.net/google/reflowlist/0.8.1/extension/package.json"}
tmplAuth="vscode-unpkg.net" reqAuth=undefined
```

That also explains why no client-side change helps: the request authority is always empty, whatever
the client sends, so every asset fails identically.

### Fix

`o.substring(uC.length)` becomes `o.substring(uC.length + 1)`.

Verified against a clean 1.134.0-insider tree: patch that one call, restart the server, and

| Asset | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `google/reflowlist/0.8.1/extension/package.json` | 403 | 200, 3576 bytes |
| `google/reflowlist/0.8.1/extension/dist/web/extension.js` | 403 | 200, 4494 bytes |
| `yzhang/markdown-all-in-one/3.6.3/extension/package.json` | 403 | 200, 33389 bytes |
| `samuelcolvin/jinjahtml/0.20.0/extension/package.json` | 403 | 200, 17181 bytes |

all matching the byte counts a direct fetch returns. Installing a web extension from the Extensions
panel then completes and the extension runs.

The `_handleStatic` branch immediately above has the same shape and the same omission, but there the
remainder is resolved against a local directory, where a leading slash is absorbed by the path join,
so only the extension-resource branch is affected.

### Impact

No web extension can be installed from the Extensions panel in any self-hosted `serve-web` /
`serve-local` deployment. Installing over the CLI (`code --install-extension`) still works, because
that path does not use this endpoint, and the extension then loads over
`/vscode-remote-resource?path=...`, which is unaffected.

title: agentHost: make startup session discovery registry-first
body:
agentHost: make startup session discovery registry-first (#331155)

A 2026-08-17 Insiders reproduction with 941 SDK sessions and 1,437
per-session databases (~946 MB) showed the ~60s delay is not migration —
`sessionRegistryBackfilled:copilotcli` was already true and migration was
skipped. The time went to per-session SQLite work during discovery and
listing: classification took 66.9s (113 external, 342 adoptable
extension-host, 486 already known), registration of the 113 emitted
candidates another 21.9s, and the first two AHP `listSessions` calls
109.8s and 91.0s, with a third 73.2s window after discovery.

Each measured phase is addressed:

- Classification (66.9s): discovery is now registry-first. `IAgent` gains
  an optional `setKnownSessionsFilter` seam that `AgentService` installs
  at provider registration; it answers, in one registry query for the
  whole candidate set, which sessions the host already owns.
  `CopilotAgent` drops those candidates instead of opening a session
  database each, so the 486 already-known sessions cost no DB opens.
  Tombstoned sessions are absent from the registry and therefore never
  reported as known, so an explicitly deleted session still reaches
  `register`, whose atomic tombstone check declines it. Provenance of a
  registered row stays owned by the explicit create/restore paths.

- Classification (the 342 adoptable rows): while migrate-legacy is off,
  adoptable extension-host candidates are never emitted, so their
  Git-touching project resolution is now skipped entirely instead of
  being computed and then filtered away. `_emitCopilotChats` keeps its
  filter as a re-check, since the setting can flip mid-pass.

- Registration (21.9s): `_registerDiscoveredChats` rejects an
  already-registered candidate with unchanged provenance before
  `_isChatBacking()` or any other per-session I/O.

- Listing (109.8s / 91.0s / 73.2s): `listSessions()` coalesces concurrent
  computations per external-sessions mode, so the burst a multi-window
  restore produces shares one registry traversal. The shared entry
  records the registry epoch it started at and every registry mutation
  invalidates it, so a caller arriving after a mutation starts a fresh
  pass rather than joining a possibly pre-mutation one. Each caller gets
  its own array; rejections are shared only with callers already waiting.

- `_readStoredSessionMetadata` / `_readSessionMetadata` now issue one
  bulk `getMetadataObject()` query instead of nine and six single-key
  reads, shrinking the cost of the fallback path that runs when no host
  filter is installed.

Deferred deliberately: seeding a newly discovered external session as
read still creates its database purely to hold one flag. Dropping the
write without a durable default would flip every discovered external
session to unread, because the list overlay only applies `IsRead` when
the key is present. The correct default belongs on the registry row and
is left to the registry list-projection change; the reasoning is
recorded on `_initializeExternalSessionReadState`. Removal of
`_awaitInitialProviderMigration()` is likewise not attempted: the
reproduction proves migration was already skipped.

Tests assert call/open counts rather than wall-clock thresholds:
registry-known candidates cause zero session DB opens; disabled
adoptable candidates resolve no projects; re-registering a known
discovered chat performs no per-session I/O; the known-sessions filter
reports registered sessions only and leaves tombstones to registration;
concurrent list calls share one computation but not their arrays; a
mutation during an in-flight list is not served from it; and stored
metadata is read with a single bulk query.

title: Modern UI: Add CSS styles to persist tab actions when action space is reserved
body:
This pull request improves the behavior and appearance of tab actions in the editor when the reserved action column is always present. **Tab Action Visibility and Interactivity Improvements:**

* Updated `tabs.css` to ensure that when the reserved action column is present (`tab-actions-reserve-space`), tab actions remain visible and clickable, with opacity adjusted based on the active/inactive state of the editor group. This prevents the reserved column from appearing empty and addresses a related issue.

**Testing Enhancements:**

* Added a test in `styleOverrides.contribution.test.ts` to verify that tab actions persist and have the correct opacity when the action space is reserved, covering active and inactive states.

title: Markdown syntax highlighting: line-leading `$` starts a math block and affects the rest of the document
body: ## Description In a Markdown document, a line beginning with a single dollar sign is interpreted as the start of a multiline math block. If the line does not contain a closing `$`, the remaining document is highlighted incorrectly. Headings and other Markdown syntax after that line lose their normal highlighting. This commonly affects Markdown containing shell prompts, commands, or environment variables. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Launch a fresh VS Code window with all extensions disabled: ```sh code --disable-extensions --new-window vscode-markdown-dollar-repro.md ``` 2. Open a Markdown file containing: ```markdown # Before $ echo "hello" # After **This should be bold** ``` 3. Compare the highlighting before and after the line beginning with `$`. ## Actual behaviour The leading `$` starts a multiline math scope. The remainder of the document is highlighted as math until another dollar sign is encountered, so `# After` and the bold text are no longer highlighted as Markdown. ## Expected behavior A line-leading `$` that does not form a closed math expression should remain ordinary Markdown text and must not affect tokenisation of subsequent lines. ## Environment - VS Code: 1.133.0 - Commit: `a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960` - Architecture: arm64 - OS: macOS 26.5.1 (25F80) - Extensions disabled: Yes - VS Code Insiders: Not tested ## Additional context This appears related to: - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/136535 - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-markdown-tm-grammar/issues/148 Issue #136535 fixed the case where `$` is followed by a digit, such as `$12.45`. The current single-dollar block rule still treats lines such as `$ command`, `$PATH`, or `$foo` as the beginning of a multiline math block: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/markdown-math/syntaxes/md-math-block.tmLanguage.json#L48-L50 The relevant rule is: ```regex (?<=^\s*)(\$)(?![^$]*\$|\d) ```

title: fix: chat respect disableAIFeatures in standalone web
body:
In standalone web without a remote authority, `ChatEntitlementService` skips creating `ChatEntitlementContext`. `AccountPolicyGateContribution` later calls `setForceHidden(false)` for an inactive gate, and the fallback directly resets
  `chatSetupHidden`, making the Chat view visible despite `chat.disableAIFeatures: true`.

  This adds `config.chat.disableAIFeatures` to the Chat view's `when` condition so the view is hidden when disabled and restored when the setting is false.

title: Add .agents/agents folder support for custom agents
body:
## Description

Custom agent files (`*.agent.md`) can currently only be defined in `.github/agents` or `.claude/agents`. This adds support for the generic `.agents/agents` convention (workspace and `~/.agents/agents` for user profile), matching the existing `.agents/skills` support.

Changes:
- `promptFileLocations.ts`: added `.agents/agents` (and `~/.agents/agents`) to `DEFAULT_AGENT_SOURCE_FOLDERS`, reusing the existing `PromptFileSource.AgentsWorkspace`/`AgentsPersonal` sources; `isInAgentsFolder()` now recognizes plain `.md` files placed there.
- `chat.shared.contribution.ts`: added `.agents/agents` to the `chat.agents.locations` setting default.
- `chatSettings.ts` / `editFileToolUtils.tsx`: added `**/.agents/agents/**` to the always-confirm edit patterns, since agent files can declare shell-executing `hooks:`.
- Added/updated unit tests covering the new location.

Fixes #329807 partly (that issue also asks for `.claude`-style `rules`/instructions support under `.agents`, which is not covered by this PR).

## How to test

1. Create a workspace folder `.agents/agents/my-agent.agent.md` with agent frontmatter (`description`, etc.).
2. Open the Chat view's agent picker — the new agent should be listed alongside any `.github/agents` or `.claude/agents` agents.
3. Run the unit tests in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/config/promptFileLocations.test.ts`, `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionPermissions.test.ts`, and `extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/test/editFileToolUtils.spec.ts`.

title: agentHost: address agent merge review feedback
body:
Follow-up to #331010, addressing the review comments left on that PR after it was merged.

### Setting rename

The Agent Merge settings no longer carry `agentHost` in their ID:

`chat.agentHost.agentMerge.*` -> `chat.agentMerge.*`

### Security

- The host now owns `agentMerge.controller` session config. `SessionConfigChanged` actions coming from a client that target host-written keys are rejected, so a client cannot forge a controller state (target, enabledAt, watermark, budgets) that later makes the gate return `confirmed: true` and triggers a native merge. Covered by two regression tests.
- `_canRepairFork` fails closed when head repository provenance is missing.
- Refs pointing at a different GitHub host are ignored.

### Correctness

- Injected autonomy configuration is reconciled on every cycle instead of once, and keys revoked by policy are rolled back. Configuration is never widened while a turn is active.
- The merge target is revalidated before starting a turn and again before merging; the merge step re-reads live state, config, target and top-level comments.
- `AgentMergeRepairAction` is split out of `AgentMergeAction` so repair paths cannot express a merge.
- Stopping the runtime cancels the controller's in-flight turn.

### Prompt bounding

Review threads now carry all of their feedback comments rather than only the first, and the prompt is bounded by explicit per-section caps plus a 20k character aggregate budget.

### Commands

Enable/disable commands have separate preconditions driven by a dedicated context key, and the configure quick pick exposes reset as a title button rather than a list entry.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run eslint`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- Agent Host unit tests (308 passing)

title: Copilot Agent Host sessions take ~60 seconds to appear after restart with a large ~/.copilot catalog

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
## Description

After restarting VS Code Insiders (1.134.0-insider, commit fc62850c), Copilot sessions in the Agents window take ~60 seconds to appear. Local harness sessions appear immediately.

## Reproduction

Machine has ~1,207 SDK sessions under `~/.copilot/session-state` and 1,373 Agent Host session databases.

## Trace from `agenthost.log`

```
09:09:44 – Copilot provider registers, begins "Listing discoverable chats"
09:09:45 – 9 concurrent listSessions() calls arrive from restored windows
09:09:54 – Copilot SDK returns 1,207 sessions
09:10:30 – _discoverCopilotChats() classification finishes (0 external, 117 adoptable legacy, 1090 already known)
09:10:45 – first live listSessions() returns 47 sessions (~60 s after startup)
```

During classification ~1,957 session database opens and then ~2,296 more during the first live list.

## Cause

`_awaitInitialProviderMigration()` in `AgentService.listSessions()` waits for the provider discovery promise before returning. The Copilot discovery pass introduced by #331082 enumerates the entire SDK catalog (~1,207 entries on this machine), classifying each one by opening its session database. The 9 concurrent `listSessions()` calls from the 8 restored windows all queue behind this discovery pass, so no Copilot sessions are shown in any window until classification completes.

The persisted `localAgentHost.cachedSessions.v2` cache contains the correct set of recent sessions and is shown immediately by other providers; Copilot sessions appear to be withheld or replaced by the live result rather than rendered from cache while discovery runs.

## Version

- VS Code Insiders 1.134.0-insider (commit `fc62850c`)
- macOS arm64

title: Fix notification close button running default action instead of dismissing
body:
When a notification has action buttons and you click the X to close it, the intent is usually to dismiss without picking an action. Instead, the close button was silently running the last primary action — same as pressing it explicitly. For destructive choices like "Delete" or "Don't Save" that's a pretty bad surprise.

title: Fix Remote Explorer showing "Server Returned 404" instead of container list
body:
After a recent update, opening the Remote Explorer sidebar with dev containers throws a "Server Returned 404" error notification and shows nothing. The extension is hitting `/v1/containers` which was removed — the service now expects `/v2/containers`.

Two changes in `containerList.ts`: updated `CONTAINER_LIST_API_PATH` to the v2 path, and added a 404 guard in `fetchDevContainers` that returns an empty array instead of propagating the error. The guard is intentionally narrow — only 404 gets swallowed, everything else still surfaces so real connectivity issues don't disappear silently. With older service versions the sidebar just shows empty rather than an error banner.

Tested against the updated endpoint (containers populate) and against a service that returns 404 (sidebar shows empty, no notification). 500s still fire the error notification.

Fixes #322795

title: Fix gopls semantic token colors in Dark Modern theme
body:
The Dark Modern theme inherits from Dark+ which inherits from the base Dark VS theme. The semantic token type `keyword` — which gopls sends for Go keywords — resolves to the `keyword.control` TextMate scope. Dark+ assigns that scope the color `#C586C0` (purple), and Dark Modern had no override for it, so Go keywords ended up purple even though every other token color in Dark Modern was updated to match the theme's revised palette.

The same applies to `function` and `method` — without explicit mappings they fall through to inherited values that weren't necessarily chosen with Dark Modern in mind.

Added a `semanticTokenColors` block to `dark_modern.json` that pins `keyword` to the blue `#569cd6` used by all other keyword-scoped tokens in the theme, and `function`/`method` to the yellow `#DCDCAA` consistent with how functions are colored everywhere else.

Tested by opening a Go file with gopls active under Dark Modern before and after the change. Keywords and function names now match the colors used by TypeScript/Python/C# in the same theme rather than inheriting the old purple tone from Dark+.

Fixes #330173

title: Please DO NOT do rounded corners.
Resolve a slash command whose content cannot be read
body:
Fixes #331138.

### Problem

In a remote window, a chat message containing a slash command never submits. The command autocompletes and renders normally, Enter does nothing, and no error reaches the UI. Reproduced with `/commit` and `/deep-research` in a dev container; the same commands work in a local window.

### Cause

`resolvePromptSlashCommand` parses the command's URI unconditionally:

```ts
const parsedPromptFile = await this.promptsService.parseNew(command.uri, token);
```

Not every command's `uri` is readable. Built-in skills are published as discovery-only entries on the `agent-builtin` scheme, carrying a name and description with nothing behind them — as `buildBuiltinSkillsContainer` states: *"the entries have no openable content"*. `parseNew` therefore rejects with `Unable to resolve nonexistent file`, and because `parsedPromptFile` is a required field the rejection escapes the resolver.

The caller is the input-decoration update, so the rejection lands on the path that produces `parsedInput`:

```
FileService.doReadFileStream
  ← parseNew
  ← resolvePromptSlashCommand
  ← updateAsyncInputEditorDecorations   (chatInputEditorContrib.ts:341)
  ← triggerInputEditorDecorationsUpdate
  ← get parsedInput ← updateChatInputContext
```

That is why the message cannot be sent and why nothing is reported: the failure is in the decoration/parse path, not in send.

The trigger is *accepting* the completion, not pressing Enter — typing the same characters without accepting the suggestion sends fine.

Local windows are unaffected only because the commands that resolve there happen to be file-backed.

### Fix

Treat parsing as best-effort and make `parsedPromptFile` optional. A command that cannot be read still resolves; only its body is unavailable. This also covers a file-backed command deleted between discovery and use, which fails identically today.

`promptFilePickers.ts` already treats a failed parse this way (`parseNew(...).catch(() => undefined)`), so this brings the two resolvers in line with existing behaviour rather than inventing a new convention.

The two consumers that dereferenced the field now skip only the part that needs a body: `chatWidget` still records prompt-run telemetry and applies header metadata when present, and `chatSessions.contribution` returns no variable entry when there is no prompt file.

### Verification

New test: a command whose content cannot be read still resolves, with `parsedPromptFile` undefined. It fails without the fix —

```
1 failing
  resolvePromptSlashCommand - unreadable command content
    Error: Unable to resolve nonexistent file
```

— and passes with it. 14613 node unit tests pass; `tsc --noEmit -p src/tsconfig.json` is clean apart from two `assignmentService.ts` errors that are present on `main` unchanged.

Also verified against a live dev-container window with the equivalent change applied to the installed build. Accepting a built-in skill completion and pressing Enter now submits. The underlying read still fails, exactly as it should for a resource with no content —

```
[warning] [RemoteAgentHostProtocol] Request 38 failed:
  {"code":-32008,"message":"Resource not found: agent-builtin:/skill/update-config"}
```

— but it is now absorbed rather than taking the submission down with it.

_Relevant TPI from last week (the `permissions` model itself): #329613_

VS Code can now auto-translate existing (legacy) VS Code settings into Copilot SDK `managedSettings.permissions` for local Agent Host sessions. This will primarily be used for policies, so existing enterprise configurations keep working in the new local agent host implementation.

The bridge is gated by `chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings` — experimental, advanced, application-machine scoped, **defaults to `false`**.

The initial mappings are:

| VS Code setting | Explicit global value | SDK contribution |
|---|---|---|
| `chat.tools.global.autoApprove` | `false` **from enterprise policy only** | `disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` |
| `chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove` | `false` | `ask: ["Shell"]` |

The mappings are declared in [`managedPermissionsSettings`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a4c94814fec1c4c12ce25d218ca0f6a3638404dc/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostManagedSettings.ts#L33-L37) — the layer that auto-translates VS Code settings into the "language" the SDK expects, namely `permissions` and its deny/ask/allow syntax. Expect this table to grow to cover the settings enterprises will have configured in legacy setups.

Only *explicitly configured* global layers are read (policy → user → application). Registered defaults and workspace/folder values are ignored by design.

## Setup

- Disposable profile and workspace.
- Enable `chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings`.
- Use **local** Agent Host sessions.
- Start a **new** Agent session after changing a setting — the contribution is read when the session is created.

## Testing

### Gating and source fidelity
- [ ] With the bridge **disabled**, neither legacy setting appears as an SDK managed restriction.
- [ ] Enable the bridge, then set `chat.tools.global.autoApprove: false` 
- [ ] Configure `chat.tools.global.autoApprove: false` through **[enterprise policy](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/enterprise/policies)** — SDK bypass mode is disabled and the user cannot override it with Allow All.
- [ ] Set `chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove: false` explicitly — Shell operations require approval through the SDK.
- [ ] A registered default (never explicitly set) contributes nothing.
- [ ] A workspace or folder value contributes nothing.


Please try additional combinations of policy changes, settings layers, and approval modes.

title: MCP App webview blank in auxiliary chat window until scroll forces reinitializeAfterDismount; mountTo registers MessagePort handler on main window before DOM node is attached to aux window
body:
MCP App webviews render correctly in the main chat panel but are completely blank when using "New Chat Window" (workbench.action.newChatWindow). The app's JavaScript never executes. Scrolling the item off-screen and back fixes it (triggers reinitializeAfterDismount()).

Root Cause:
In chatToolInvocationPart.ts, the ChatMcpAppModel is instantiated (which calls mountTo) before the domNode is placed into the auxiliary window's DOM:

```
// chatToolInvocationPart.ts ~line 247
this.mcpAppPart.value = this.instantiationService.createInstance(
    ChatMcpAppSubPart, ...  // constructor calls mountTo() immediately
);
appDomNode.replaceWith(this.mcpAppPart.value.domNode); // only NOW in aux window DOM
```
Inside ChatMcpAppModel constructor:

```
const targetWindow = dom.getWindow(this._container); // container not yet in aux window DOM → returns main window
this._webview.mountTo(this._container, targetWindow); // registers message handler on WRONG window
```

WebviewElement.mountTo() calls _registerMessageHandler(targetWindow) and sets parentOrigin from targetWindow.origin. Since targetWindow is the main window but the iframe ends up in the auxiliary window, the MessagePort handshake fails silently. The queued _send('content', ...) call never delivers the HTML.

Evidence:

Console in auxiliary window shows only the iframe sandbox warning — zero app log output (JS never executes)
reinitializeAfterDismount() (triggered by scroll off/on) calls getWindow(this.element) when the element IS in the auxiliary window DOM, fixing the window reference
Suggested Fix:
Either:

Defer mountTo() until after the domNode is attached to the target window's DOM (e.g., use queueMicrotask or move mount into a post-attach callback)
Call remount() after appDomNode.replaceWith(...) in the autorun
Pass the correct targetWindow explicitly from the ChatMcpAppSubPart constructor context (which knows the target window from dom.getWindow(this.domNode) after it's been attached by the list renderer)

Repro:

Have an MCP server with an app-enabled tool (uses x-]]mcpApps resource)
Open Chat panel → invoke the tool → renders correctly
Click + dropdown → "New Chat Window" → invoke the same tool → blank area
Scroll the chat up until the result is off-screen, then scroll back down → renders correctly

title: fix(process-explorer): report memory footprint on macOS
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #194322

## Root cause

On macOS the process explorer's memory column is derived from the `%mem` column of `ps`, which is based on the resident set size (RSS). RSS ignores compressed memory, so the values diverge significantly from what Activity Monitor shows — the issue reporter saw 4 GB for one helper process in Activity Monitor while the process explorer accounted for less than 1 GB in total.

The MEM column of macOS `top` reports the physical footprint of a process, which is the same value Activity Monitor displays (verified against `footprint -p <pid>`, which prints `phys_footprint` directly):

| process | ps RSS-based (before) | top MEM / footprint (after) |
|-|-|-|
| Google Chrome | 232 MB | 333 MB |
| Electron renderer | 457 MB | 667 MB |
| node with 256 MB Buffer | 295 MB | 268 MB |

Unlike `vmmap` (discussed in the issue), `top` is preinstalled on every macOS system, and the Linux code path is untouched.

## What changed

- After the process tree is built from `ps` output as before, darwin now runs a single `top -l 1 -stats pid,mem -pid <pid>...` invocation limited to the pids of the tree (~1s, comparable to the existing 1s CPU sampling on Linux) and overrides the memory values with the reported footprints in bytes. This also handles `top`'s `K`/`M`/`G`/`T` suffixes and the `+` compressed-memory marker.
- If `top` fails or omits a pid, the ps-derived value is kept as a fallback, so behavior degrades to the status quo instead of breaking.

## How to test

- Added unit tests for the `top` output parser in `src/vs/base/test/node/ps.test.ts` (`npm run test-node`).
- Manual: open the Process Explorer (Help > Open Process Explorer) on macOS and compare the Memory column with Activity Monitor for the same pids — the values now match Activity Monitor instead of being consistently lower.

The renderer fails to read the skill resource behind the command:

```
[error] Unable to read file 'vscode-agent-host://local/skill/commit?_ah=eyJzY2hlbWUiOiJhZ2VudC1idWlsdGluIn0'
        (Error: Unable to resolve nonexistent file 'vscode-agent-host://local/skill/commit?_ah=...')
```

(`_ah` decodes to `{"scheme":"agent-builtin"}`.)

### Repro

1. Open a folder in a dev container.
2. In the agent chat, type a message containing a slash command (`/commit`).
3. Press Enter.

Observed: nothing is submitted. `renderer.log` records the read failure above each time.

Expected: the message submits, as it does in a local window.

### What makes this look like a routing problem rather than a missing resource

The resource exists and is advertised **by the container's agent host**. Its protocol log carries 63 `agent-builtin` entries, including the exact one being read:

```
agent-builtin:/skill/commit
agent-builtin:/skill/code-review
agent-builtin:/skill/agents
agent-builtin:/skill/__remote-workflow
...
```

The host builds these without an authority ([claudeBuiltinCommands.ts:110](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/customizations/claudeBuiltinCommands.ts#L110)):

```ts
const uri = URI.from({ scheme: AGENT_BUILTIN_SCHEME, path: `/skill/${encodeURIComponent(entry.name)}` }).toString();
```

and the client turns them into `vscode-agent-host://<authority>/...`, preserving the original scheme in `_ah`. The authority it stamps is the ambient `local` ([AMBIENT_AGENT_HOST_AUTHORITY = 'local'](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostConnectionsService.ts#L31)); every one of the 40 `vscode-agent-host://` URIs in my logs uses it, and no other authority ever appears.

So a resource advertised by one host is read back under an authority that does not identify that host. In a local window the ambient host is the one that advertised it and the read succeeds; in a remote window it does not.

I have not confirmed which service the `local` authority resolves to in a remote window — `agentHostChatContribution` registers it against `_agentHostService` ([:177](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostChatContribution.ts#L177)) — so I am describing the symptom and the asymmetry rather than asserting the mechanism.

### Severity

Slash commands are unusable in remote windows, and the failure is silent from the user's point of view: the command autocompletes and renders normally, and Enter simply does nothing. There is no error surfaced in the UI and no indication that the message was not sent.

### Possibly related

#330979 — same theme of a resource being addressed to the wrong host, there for session working directories. Different code path; filing separately.

### Environment

VS Code 1.133.0 (`a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960`), Windows client, dev container remote, Claude provider. Reproduced with `/commit` and `/deep-research`; works in a local window on the same machine.

title: Normalize required semantics for ask-user questions across providers
body:
## Problem

Ordinary ask-user questions currently have inconsistent `required` semantics across agent providers. This surfaced as a confusing required `*` in the Agents Window.

`ChatInputQuestionBase` supports optional `required?: boolean`, but the source protocols do not consistently provide that information:

- Copilot SDK `UserInputRequest` has no `required` field, yet `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts` maps ordinary `ask_user` questions with `required: true` (around lines 3255-3271).
- Codex similarly sets `required: true` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/codex/codexUserInputMapper.ts` (around lines 18-41).
- Claude's ordinary `AskUserQuestion` mapper omits `required` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/claudeInteractiveTools.ts` (around lines 98-123).

In the workbench, `required` prevents advancing/submitting while a question is unanswered and adds a visible `*`. `allowSkip` still allows dismissing the entire prompt, which makes the provider-dependent asterisk especially unclear.

MCP elicitation is distinct: it correctly derives required fields from the MCP JSON Schema `required` set and should retain those schema-driven semantics.

## Expected

Ordinary ask-user questions should have normalized semantics across providers—likely optional unless the source protocol explicitly marks them required. MCP form questions should continue to derive `required` from their JSON Schema.

## Actual

Equivalent ordinary questions appear required for Copilot and Codex, but optional for Claude, based on provider-specific mapper defaults rather than source-protocol semantics.

title: agentHost: limit worktree session workspace matching to legacy CLI sessions
body:
Follow-up to #330973.

That PR added the session's server-owned `project` (repository) root as a containment candidate when deciding whether a session belongs to the current workspace. That made *every* worktree-isolated session show up in an editor window opened on its repository folder — including agent-host worktree sessions, which was decided not to support in the editor window going forward. 

This narrows the fallback: the project root is only used as a matching candidate for legacy Copilot CLI sessions (those carrying the
`ehcliAdoptable` marker). All other sessions fall back to working-directory containment, so new worktree sessions stay out of the editor window.

No behavior change for the Agents window, which runs workspace-less and listsall sessions regardless.

title: Add git.copyChanges command to Source Control panel
body:
Related to #333843

## Summary
- Adds a new `git.copyChanges` command to the Source Control panel that copies the current repository's changes (staged, unstaged, and untracked) to the clipboard, formatted per file.

title: Agent Host: first-turn config refresh leaves new chat permanently active

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: N/A (built-in Agent Host)
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0-insider
- OS Version: macOS 26.6.1 arm64
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent mode, new worktree-isolated session
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Agent Host debug bundle captured locally. The bundle did not include the Copilot runtime process log containing the terminal failure, so the relevant redacted excerpt from `process-1786891402662-64463.log` is included below. Affected Copilot CLI runtime: 1.0.79.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create a new worktree-isolated Agent Host session with active client tools and synced customizations.
2. Send the first prompt so the provisional chat materializes while the worktree-scoped customization bundle is republished.
3. Observe that the chat remains active indefinitely with no assistant response or terminal error.

## Expected

The first turn completes normally, or a runtime failure produces a terminal `chat/error`/`chat/turnComplete` transition so the UI stops showing the chat as active.

## Actual

The turn remains permanently active. In the captured run:

- Host session: `copilotcli:/98345434-f968-419e-bc34-dd191b28e382`
- SDK session: `265899d1-d87c-4303-b143-26355624c196`
- Turn: `request_dec9bbae-59c0-463b-99d4-015c2a95d36b`

The AHP turn opened optimistically at `20:24:57.249Z`, before an SDK session existed. The provisional SDK session was created at `20:25:01.105Z`. Its worktree-scoped synced-customization bundle was then republished with a new content nonce while the client tool set remained unchanged. During the same first-send call, `ActiveClient.requiresRestart` detected the updated plugin snapshot and refreshed the session.

Agent Host log:

```text
Session configuration changed, refreshing session
SDK resumeSession failed: Session not found: 265899d1-d87c-4303-b143-26355624c196
Resume reported no session history; falling back to createSession with same ID
Fallback createSession succeeded
session.send() returned
```

Copilot runtime process log:

```text
20:25:01.105Z Created session: 265899d1-d87c-4303-b143-26355624c196
20:25:01.364Z Closing session 265899d1-d87c-4303-b143-26355624c196
20:25:01.372Z Destroyed session 265899d1-d87c-4303-b143-26355624c196 after last owner detached
20:25:01.380Z Session not found: 265899d1-d87c-4303-b143-26355624c196
20:25:01.403Z Created session: 265899d1-d87c-4303-b143-26355624c196
20:25:11.338Z Agentic loop failed: Error: CompactionProcessorHandle has already been disposed
```

No `session.error`, `session.idle`, assistant turn event, or matching AHP `chat/turnComplete` reached Agent Host afterward. The only chat actions after `chat/turnStarted` were worktree-creation activity and one response-part placeholder.

## Root cause

The primary trigger is deterministic in VS Code:

1. The first send materializes a provisional SDK session.
2. The worktree-scoped customization snapshot changes before that same send reaches the model.
3. `_sendMessageOnce` destroys the just-created empty session and attempts to resume the same SDK ID.
4. Disconnecting the last owner destroys that empty runtime session, so resume reports `Session not found`.
5. `CopilotSessionLauncher` falls back to `createSession` with the same ID.

The recreated runtime then reports that its `CompactionProcessorHandle` is disposed. The logs prove the failure follows same-ID destroy/recreate, but do not prove the precise internal mechanism. The replacement may be observing state retained from the first instance, or late teardown from the first instance may be disposing a resource used by the replacement.

The runtime catches the agentic-loop failure but no terminal SDK event reaches Agent Host, leaving the optimistic AHP turn active.

## Existing hang detection

`AgentHostTurnTracker` already classifies a turn with no observed provider progress as `noProgress` after `TURN_HANG_THRESHOLD_MS` (five minutes), but this watchdog only emits telemetry. It does not terminate or recover the active turn.

## Potential fixes

1. Avoid destroy→resume for a newly materialized, unused session during its first send. Reconcile the final worktree-scoped customization snapshot before creating the SDK session, or recreate the empty backing without reusing the destroyed runtime identity.
2. Use the existing `AgentHostTurnTracker` no-progress watchdog as a recovery hook so a lost provider turn cannot remain active indefinitely.
3. Harden same-ID session recreation in the Copilot runtime and ensure agentic-loop failures always produce terminal SDK events.

Unrelated MCP startup/auth warnings occurred concurrently but were not the source of the disposed-handle failure.

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: N/A (built-in Agent Host)
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0-insider, commit `43c9cf468f20acda12efca27ba820d27aacf84df`
- OS Version: macOS arm64
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents Window, `create_chat` peer chat
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Agent Host debug bundle analyzed locally. It is not attached because it may contain sensitive prompts, file contents, paths, settings, and credentials. Sanitized evidence is included below.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Run a session in the Agents Window and have it call `create_chat`, which starts a prompt in a peer chat.
2. Navigate away so the renderer unsubscribes from the parent session and its default chat while the peer chat is still executing.
3. Wait for the 30-second session-release grace period.
4. Observe that the peer chat appears to stop, although the Copilot SDK continues running tools and producing events.

Expected: The parent session remains live until every catalog chat is idle, or the peer chat continues to receive and persist events while it is active.

Actual: The host evicts the parent session's cached state after the grace period. All subsequent peer-chat events are discarded as actions for an unknown chat, so the UI stops updating even though provider execution continues.

Sanitized timeline:

- `20:46:21.503`: peer chat backing is created under session `copilotcli:/9bd…`.
- `20:46:21.516`: peer chat status changes to `InProgress`.
- `20:46:39.327`: client unsubscribes from the parent session and default chat.
- `20:47:09.328`: `[AgentService] Evicting idle session ... (triggered by unsubscribe ...)`.
- `20:47:23.474` onward: `[AgentHostStateManager] Action for unknown chat ...`; tool calls and deltas continue for several minutes but are dropped from host state.

Root cause:

In the affected build, `AgentService._maybeEvictIdleSession` only guards on `targetState.activeTurn` / `settledState.activeTurn`, which reflects the default chat. A concurrently running peer chat is therefore missed. The method then removes the session and every owned chat before asking the provider to release them. Copilot's release implementation notices that the peer chat still has an active turn and leaves the SDK session running, but the host-side chat state has already been removed.

Current `main` contains commit `962cde6575e27bdcf58c8aa2d411ae5170c31e88` from #330132, which adds a per-chat `canReleaseChat` preflight before evicting state. The affected Insiders build predates that commit. This issue tracks verification that the fix reaches Insiders and covers the active peer-chat navigation scenario.

## Summary

Adds a bounded `currentStage` property to `agentHost.turnHung` so unexpected hangs can be separated across working-directory resolution, model selection, send preparation, and provider execution. New and resumed subagent turns are attributed directly to provider execution.

## Motivation

On the latest complete UTC day (2026-08-15), Copilot 1.134.0 Insiders recorded 20.938 unexpected hangs per 1,000 messages versus 13.597 on Stable 1.133.0. Linux `noProgress` remained elevated at 8.104 per 1,000 eligible messages versus 2.929 on Windows. Additionally, 56 of 83 1.134.0 Insider incidents (67.5%) followed `chat.usage` or `chat.toolCallComplete`.

The new field distinguishes incidents that have not reached the provider boundary from provider lifecycle stalls without collecting prompts, paths, errors, or other content.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- 34 targeted Agent Host telemetry tests

- VS Code Version: Insiders/main containing 731506386b35

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Keep a previously discovered Agent Host dev tunnel cached while its remote host is offline.
2. Focus or refocus the VS Code window.
3. Observe `[TunnelAgentHost] Connect to <host> failed: Error: No hosts are currently accepting connections for the tunnel.` in the developer console.
4. Refocus again after the 10-second rate limit and observe another connection attempt and warning.

Expected: An offline tunnel remains paused until tunnel discovery confirms that its host is online.

title: Add ESLint rule for command title capitalizatio
body:
Implements #243333 by adding a new ESLint rule that validates command titles follow Microsoft title-style capitalization guidelines.

## Changes
- Added `code-command-title-capitalization.ts` ESLint rule
- Added comprehensive test file with valid/invalid cases
- Updated `eslint.config.js` to register the new rule

## Rule Behavior
The rule validates that command titles follow Microsoft title-style capitalization:
- Articles (a, an, the) are lowercase unless first/last word
- Prepositions of 4 or fewer letters are lowercase unless first/last word  
- Conjunctions (and, but, or, nor, yet, so) are lowercase unless first/last word
- All other words are capitalized (first letter uppercase, rest lowercase)
- Hyphenated words are handled correctly
- Case normalization handles ALL CAPS and mixed case inputs

## Reference
Microsoft Style Guide: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/capitalization#title-style-capitalization

title: agentHost: Stabilize reconnect E2E tests
body:
Fixes the reconnect E2E flake observed in [Azure build 465101](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=465101).

The reconnect scenarios accidentally reused the shared client identity for the transport they deliberately dropped. Until the server processed the close event, that newer transport could receive the action echo instead of the shared client, leaving the test to hit its 30-second notification timeout. Give each dropped transport an explicitly distinct logical client ID.

Validation:
- `npm run compile`
- `npm run hygiene`
- formerly flaky focused test passed 50/50 fresh-process runs after reproducing the original failure on iteration 8
- complete Agent Host conformance suite: 260 passing, 15 expected pending

title: Support keyboard Layout on Linux
body: VS Code for the Web supports Keyboard Layout to manually define the keyboard layout used by VS Code. It would be useful to provide the same functionality in the Linux desktop version, allowing users to configure or override the detected keyboard layout when it is incorrect. For consistency with the web version, Linux should provide a way to create and configure `keyboardLayout.json`, ideally with the same **Configure Keyboard Layout** workflow. ```json { "keyboard.layout": "es" } ```

title: sessions: Stabilize docked side pane sizing
body:
## Summary

- make docked Details take its width from Sessions while preserving the pure Editor-content width
- keep side-pane geometry stable across reloads, session switches, detail-only layouts, sash reset, and whole-pane closure
- coordinate Existing Session close/profile transitions so intermediate compositions are not persisted
- add regression coverage and document the single-pane sizing contract

## Why

The docked Auxiliary Bar shares the Editor grid node. Some visibility transitions treated the combined Editor+Details width as pure Editor width, while others restored a composition-specific width after Details had already hidden. Repeating those transitions caused the side pane to grow or shrink cumulatively.

The sizing state now distinguishes pure Editor width from combined composition width and restores each only in the matching composition.

- all five affected Sessions workbench/layout/strategy suites

title: Force commit messages output to UTF-8
body: Fixes #331086 ## Summary I modified the code to enforce the `i18n.logOutputEncoding=UTF-8` setting when calling Git. ## Test The test I added checks whether commit messages written in an encoding other than UTF-8 (EUC-JP) are retrieved as UTF-8. Without my fix, they would be retrieved as EUC-JP, causing the test to fail. ## Image ## Additional Information Even after applying this setting, my local test results showed that the execution time remained unchanged. I conducted the following experiment in the vscode repository. If no settings are specified ```console $ time for i in $(seq 1 10) ;do git --no-pager log >& /tmp/output.txt ; done real 0m12.062s user 0m11.392s sys 0m0.647s ``` If a setting is specified ```console $ time for i in $(seq 1 10) ;do git --no-pager -c i18n.logOutputEncoding=UTF-8 log >& /tmp/output.txt ; done real 0m11.824s user 0m11.034s sys 0m0.768s ```
